name: Mucomuscular flap lip augmentation

card.summary: Surgical lip enlargement by moving intraoral tissue into the lip; the only source reviewed describes flaps generally as adding little volume.
card.note: Very thin sourcing: no studies specific to this technique were found.

quick.overview:
Surgical flap procedures move small strips of tissue from near the lips or inside the mouth into the lip. Wikipedia says this adds little volume and gives only slight protrusion.

No studies specific to mucomuscular flap augmentation were found, and the registered trials surfaced under this name concern dental implants and bone grafting.
quick.mechanism: A strip of mucosa and underlying muscle is repositioned within the lip to increase bulk.
quick.risks: General lip surgery risks listed on Wikipedia include bleeding, swelling, uneven lips and lumpiness; no figures for this technique were found.

lead: Mucomuscular flap lip augmentation is a surgical way to make the lips fuller by repositioning the patient's own tissue, a strip of mucosa and underlying muscle from inside the mouth, into the lip. People consider it as a permanent alternative to fillers, because it uses their own tissue rather than an injected or implanted material. [1]

Wikipedia's lip augmentation article places flaps alongside fillers, implants and fat grafting: small sections of skin near the lips or inside the mouth are moved to the lips, a technique it says adds little volume and gives only slight protrusion. [1] Fuller, more defined lips are what patients usually seek from lip augmentation of any kind. [1]
Published literature on mucosal and myomucosal lip flaps mostly concerns reconstruction after cancer removal, trauma or congenital defects rather than cosmetic enlargement. [2][3]

angle.text: The procedure aims to add bulk and slight projection to the lips using the patient's own tissue, giving a permanent option compared with fillers that are absorbed over months. [1]

infobox: Patient's own intraoral mucosa and muscle [1]

paras: Flap techniques differ from fillers and implants in using the patient's own nearby tissue rather than an injected or implanted material. [1] In the surrounding lip augmentation literature, fillers include bovine collagen, hyaluronic acid products such as Restylane and Juvederm, and calcium hydroxylapatite; implants include expanded PTFE strips; and fat grafting is rated by several studies among the best options for a semi-permanent result. [1]
Wikipedia describes flap augmentation as adding little volume with only slight protrusion, which is the main reason cited for other methods being more common. [1]

Myomucosal flaps are established in lip reconstruction. A Brazilian series of 17 men used a vermilion myomucosal advancement flap, advancing the oral orbicularis muscle and mucosa, to repair lower-lip defects after tumour removal; it reported no infection, flap necrosis or need for revision, with three cases of microstomia. [2] A report of nasolabial flaps for lip reconstruction paired them with vermilion advancement, hinged buccal mucosal or mucosal V-Y advancement flaps and reported satisfactory aesthetic and functional results in five patients. [3] These are reconstructive settings, not cosmetic augmentation.

General lip surgery and augmentation risks listed on Wikipedia include bleeding, swelling, uneven lips and lumpiness, and results depend heavily on the provider's skill. [1] No complication figures specific to cosmetic mucomuscular flap augmentation were found.

No studies found on cosmetic mucomuscular flap lip augmentation. Related reconstruction studies of vermilion myomucosal and nasolabial flaps exist, in small case series after cancer resection, trauma or congenital defects. [2][3]
